note: NTD = neglected tropical diseases (19 GBD causes, excluding malaria); DALY = disability-adjusted life-year; UI = uncertainty interval. Rates are age-standardised DALYs per 100 000 population. title: Spatial Autocorrelation and Socioeconomic Inequality in Age-Standardised DALY Rates, 2023
note: Moran's I and local indicators of spatial association (LISA) computed on log(1 + rate) with row-standardised k = 6 nearest-neighbour weights and 9 999 permutations; LISA clusters reported at Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate q<0.05 (n = 203 countries with geometry). Concentration index is population-weighted, ranking countries by Socio-demographic Index (SDI); negative values indicate burden concentrated in low-SDI countries; 95% CI from 2 000 bootstrap resamples. Theil T is population-weighted (GBD populations) over countries with a non-zero rate (NTDs n = 204; malaria n = 86) and decomposed into between- and within-super-region components; Table S15b gives the three-level decomposition and Table S22 the sensitivity to population source and zero rates.

title: Association Between External (Donor) Share of Health Expenditure and Age-Standardised DALY Rates Across Estimators
note: Estimates are percentage changes in the age-standardised DALY rate per 10-percentage-point increase in the external share of current health expenditure, adjusted for income (log LDI), UHC index, basic sanitation and drinking-water coverage, and (panel models) log domestic government health spending per capita; panel exposures lagged 2 years. NTD models: low- and middle-income countries (LMICs); malaria models: malaria-endemic LMICs. n = countries (cross-section) or country-years (panel). FE = fixed effects; CRE = correlated random effects; SAR = spatial autoregressive; SEM = spatial error model. Spatial panel models include country and year fixed effects (balanced panels; KNN k = 6 weights); SAR rows show the coefficient β, with direct, indirect and total associations in Table S12. Preferred estimator selected on the basis of Hausman and Mundlak tests (rejecting random effects) and evidence of cross-sectional dependence, serial correlation and heteroskedasticity (Table S3), for which Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are robust.

title: Projected Excess Annual DALYs Under Development-Assistance Cut Scenarios, Low- and Middle-Income Countries
cols: Accounting model: excess DALYs, thousands [95% UI]
Econometric model: excess DALYs, thousands [95% UI]
note: Accounting ("gains-at-risk") model: excess = reduction in all-age DALY rate 2010–2023 × 2023 population × external share of health expenditure × proportional cut; GBD uncertainty propagated through 4 000 Monte Carlo draws with rank-correlated 2010/2023 draws and cut magnitude sampled uniformly within the scenario range. Econometric model: preferred two-way FE (Driscoll–Kraay) coefficient applied to the cut-induced fall in external share. The reference range brackets the IHME preliminary 22% decline in global development assistance for health, 2024–2025. Economic value at 1 × GDP per capita per DALY (see Table S7 for 0.5× and 3×). Estimates represent the annual burden associated with reversal of donor-attributable gains, not first-year effects.

title: Extent and Pattern of Missing Data in the Panel Modelling Frame (LMICs, 2007–2022)
note: Frame: 168 LMICs × 16 years = 2,688 country-years. Rule: within-country linear interpolation of interior gaps and last observation carried forward for at most 2 years; no backward extrapolation, no cross-country borrowing, outcomes never imputed. Complete-case rows for the NTD model: 2,287 (85.1%) from 153 countries, of which 76 (3.3%) contain ≥1 filled value. Incompleteness was associated with lower burden (OR 0.33 per log unit, 95% CI 0.12–0.91) and earlier years (OR 0.94 per year), not with SDI (logistic model, country-clustered SE), consistent with missingness at random conditional on observed covariates. The 14 territories never reporting external health expenditure hold 0.77% of LMIC NTD DALYs.

title: Socioeconomic Inequality in Age-Standardised DALY Rates by Socio-demographic Index, 1990, 2010 and 2023
cols: Slope index of inequality, per 100 000 [95% CI]
note: All 204 countries and territories, weighted by GBD population (1990) or population implied by GBD all-age counts and crude rates (2010, 2023), ranked by SDI of the same year. Concentration index ranges from −1 to 1; negative values indicate burden concentrated in low-SDI countries. The slope index of inequality (SII) is the population-weighted regression slope of the age-standardised rate on the fractional SDI rank (ridit), that is, the modelled difference between the highest- and lowest-SDI ends of the distribution; relative SII = SII ÷ population-weighted mean. 95% CI from 2 000 bootstrap resamples of countries; changes use paired resampling, so a change is distinguishable from zero when its interval excludes zero. NTD rates are NTDs and malaria minus malaria. 2023 values can differ from Table 2 in the second decimal because Table 2 weights by World Bank population and excludes zero rates from Theil T.
